author: John Stuart Mill
title: On Liberty
edition: Fourth edition (London: Longmans, Green, Reader, and Dyer, 1869). Scan-backed Wikisource transcription. Prose line wrapping is collapsed within retained paragraphs; HTML emphasis becomes plain text. Printed page numbers, navigation, footnote reference markers, and zero-width page-boundary characters are omitted; main-text wording and punctuation are retained. Original verse line breaks are preserved where present. Apparent errors present in the linked transcription are retained rather than silently corrected; this extraction check is not a fresh complete print-image collation. The library text holds the Humboldt epigraph, Mill's dedication and Chapters I to V with their printed titles, ending with THE END; the title page, contents and printer's colophon are omitted, and so are Mill's nine footnotes (five in Chapter II, three in Chapter III, one in Chapter IV).

rights.basis: This original English edition was published in 1869, before 1931, and is public domain in the United States as of 2026. The linked scan index identifies the printed edition; no modern editorial material is supplied.

acquisition.method: Wikisource rendered page HTML (index.php action=render) for the main page and its five chapter subpages in printed order, On Liberty and On Liberty/Chapter 1 to Chapter 5 (revisions 16132207, 3944546, 8111605, 8203199, 8246968, 8253810); downloadSha256 is the SHA-256 of the six responses concatenated in that order and downloadUrl the first of them. Only the transcluded scan text is used, from the epigraph on: Wikisource headers, page-number anchors, footnote markers and lists, and zero-width page-boundary characters removed; centred chapter numbers and titles became headings; paragraphs joined with whitespace collapsed to single spaces and emphasis flattened.
